Medical Centers

Three controls validated for clinical and research scenarios

These controls are part of this integrated guide. They were tested with synthetic identifiers and documents in a Microsoft test tenant; no patient or production data was used.

P1 — Block clinical prompts

Detects a medical record number (MRN) with a sensitive information type (SIT) and a keyword condition, then blocks the prompt.

DIAX-LAB-Cowork-01-Block-Clinical-Prompts
Where tested: Copilot Chat
Result: T1 positive prompt matched; the negative control did not. T8a confirmed the rule did not apply to a user outside the Testers group.
Open P1 lab evidence

P2 — Suppress sensitive web searches

Uses a research-protocol SIT and keyword condition to suppress external web grounding. Copilot can still respond from permitted sources.

DIAX-LAB-Cowork-02-Block-Sensitive-WebSearch
Where tested: Cowork
Result: Activity Explorer later showed matches aligned with both T2 runs. T8b confirmed the rule did not apply to a user outside the Testers group.
Open P2 lab evidence

P3 — Exclude restricted files

Uses a sensitivity-label condition to exclude matching clinical or research files from Copilot grounding.

DIAX-LAB-Cowork-03-Exclude-Restricted-Grounding
Where tested: Cowork
Result: T4 and T5 passed after label metadata was repopulated. T8c-1 passed outside the Testers group; T8c-2 remained inconclusive.
Open P3 lab evidence

Evidence boundaries

  • P1 was tested in Copilot Chat; P2 and P3 were tested in Cowork.
  • P3 behavioral retests passed, but audit corroboration of those specific retests was still pending when the report was written.
  • The P3 investigation observed empty SharePoint label metadata followed by passing retests after labels were reapplied. The exact synchronization mechanism was not independently confirmed.
  • Validate the rules, scope, licensing, and propagation behavior in your own tenant before enforcement.
